prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
Sorry to hear you were in an accident — that’s stressful. I can’t pick a single lawyer for you without more details, but I can help you choose the right one and even put together a shortlist if you tell me more. First, a few quick questions:

- Where in Pleasanton are you (zip code)?  
- What were your injuries (minor, fractures, head injury, long-term disability)?  
- Was it a car vs. car collision, hit-and-run, uninsured/underinsured motorist, or something else?  
- Have you already talked to your insurance company or received a settlement offer?  
- Any deadline concerns (doctor cleared, insurer pressing you, lawsuit already filed)?

Key things to know and do right now
- Get medical care and follow-up. Document every visit.  
- Preserve evidence: photos of vehicles/scene/injuries, dashcam, witness names/contacts, police report number.  
- Don’t give recorded statements to the other driver’s insurer without your lawyer.  
- California’s personal injury statute of limitations is generally 2 years from the accident (Civ. Proc. Code §335.1)—don’t delay finding counsel if your case may require a lawsuit.

How to choose the right lawyer — what to look for
- Experience with car-accident/personal-injury cases (not general practice).  
- Trial experience and a track record of taking cases to verdict (good for avoiding lowball offers).  
- Local experience (Pleasanton/Alameda County courts, local medical providers, investigators).  
- Clear contingency fee terms (typical ranges: ~33% pre-litigation, higher if suit filed—confirm exact terms).  
- Resources to handle medical liens, experts, accident reconstruction, and upfront case costs.  
- Good communication: returns calls, explains strategy, sets expectations.  
- Clean disciplinary record (verify at calbar.ca.gov).  
- Client reviews and peer ratings (Avvo, Martindale-Hubbell, Google reviews) — view with caution but useful for patterns.

What to ask at a consultation (bring your documents)
Documents to bring: police report, photos, medical records/summary, insurance info, correspondence from insurers, and notes about the accident.
Questions:
- What percentage of your practice is car-accident/personal-injury work?  
- How many similar cases have you handled and what were typical outcomes?  
- Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee and what costs will I be responsible for?  
- Do you try cases or mostly settle? How often do you go to trial?  
- Who in your firm will handle my case day-to-day? How will I get updates?  
- What is your estimate of value and timeline based on my facts?  
- Can you provide references from former clients?  
- Have you ever been disciplined by the State Bar?

Red flags to avoid
- Promises of a specific settlement amount or “guaranteed” outcome.  
- Pressure to sign immediately without reading the agreement.  
- Unwillingness to put fees in writing or clarify costs.  
- Poor communication during the initial contact.

Next steps I can help with
- If you want, give me your zip code and a few preferences (languages, budget, whether you want a large firm or solo), and I’ll prepare a short checklist and a sample shortlist of types of attorneys to contact (you can then verify current status and reviews).  
- I can also draft a short phone script or email to send to firms for your initial consult.

If you share more details about your accident and what’s most important to you (quick settlement vs. max recovery, trial-ready, local vs. larger firm), I’ll tailor the recommendations.
